drafted_from: tools/keep-and-wake-ai-sessions-on-this-computer/what-this-tool-does-and-how-to-run-it.json (tool:start-a-codex-run-on-this-computer), harness/codex-runs.mjs (startCodexRun and its command line), test/codex-runs.test.mjs
start_here: Say to your AI: "Start a Codex run in my folder ~/projects/demo with the prompt in the file ~/prompts/hello.txt." It starts Codex in that folder on this computer and answers a run id; read it with the read row.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list of yours: it starts one Codex run in a folder you name, with a prompt you name in a file, and writes only its own run folder.
instructions: 1. Put the prompt in a plain text file, not empty, outside the repository.
2. Name the folder Codex runs in; it must exist on this computer.

3. The AI runs node tools/keep-and-wake-ai-sessions-on-this-computer/harness/codex-runs.mjs start --folder <folder> --message-file <file> from the root of the Workshop checkout. The prompt is read from the file, never from the command line.
4. Keep the run id it answers; read the run with tool:read-a-codex-run-on-this-computer, and stop it only when you ask with tool:cancel-a-codex-run-on-this-computer.

worked_examples.title: Start a one-line Codex run
worked_examples.ask: Start Codex in ~/projects/demo with the prompt in ~/prompts/hello.txt.
worked_examples.given: A folder that exists and a prompt file that is not empty.
